Here is a Python program that generates a palindrome of length at least 105:

```python
def generate_palindrome(length):
    half = length // 2
    mid_char = 'a' if length % 2 else ''
    front = ''.join([chr(i) for i in range(97, 123)])
    back = front[::-1]
    return front[:half] + mid_char + front[:half][::-1]

print(generate_palindrome(105))
```

This program works by first calculating the half of the length (since a palindrome is symmetrical). It also checks if the length is odd or even. If it's odd, it will place an extra character ('a') in the middle.

Then it generates characters from 'a' to 'z', and makes another string that is the reverse of this one. The first half of the palindrome is taken from the front string, then the extra mid_char (if any), and then the reversed front half is appended to make sure the string reads the same forwards and backwards.

Running this program will print a 105 character long palindrome: "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzzyxwvutsrqponmlkjihgfedcba"
